_README: Tips, myths and culture posts: no venue data needed. Used in order, one per story day (see storyDays in config.json), then it starts again. kind 'myths' = slides with myth + truth; kind 'list' = slides with title + body. {city} is swapped in. 'question' ends the caption to get comments; 'note' (optional) is added to the caption, for health topics. Style: all lowercase, no emojis, a blustering, posh, over-the-top old-school politician voice (cripes, piffle, latin, 'folks'). Never name or quote a real person. Facts stay accurate: health claims say 'linked with', never 'cures'. Dublin: each story has have a 'dublin' block (hook, subhook, question, note, slides) that replaces those fields on Dublin days. The Dublin voice is irish, not posh english: cap, bad craic, grand, deadly, notions, fair play, sure look, lads.

stories.hook: how to do a sauna session properly
stories.question: how many rounds do you do?

slides.title: 1. heat
slides.body: 8–15 minutes in the sauna. bail out sooner if you fancy. no medals awarded.

slides.title: 2. cold
slides.body: cold shower, plunge pool or fresh air. even 30 seconds counts. brace yourself.

slides.title: 3. rest
slides.body: sit or lie down for 10–15 minutes and drink some water. frankly, the best bit.

slides.title: 4. repeat
slides.body: two to four rounds is the classic. then finish however your heart desires.

stories.hook: sauna etiquette: don't be this person
stories.question: what's the worst sauna etiquette you've seen?

slides.title: skipping the shower
slides.body: rinse off before you go in. a small step for you, a giant leap for everyone else.

slides.title: no towel on the bench
slides.body: always sit on your own towel. always. i cannot stress this enough.

slides.title: throwing water without asking
slides.body: more steam means more heat for everyone. consult the room. democracy!

slides.title: holding the door open
slides.body: all the heat escapes. in and out, briskly, like a man late for a vote.

slides.title: the loud phone call
slides.body: if you must bring it, silence it. better still, abandon it in the locker.

stories.hook: what science actually says about saunas

stories.note: not medical advice. pregnant, have a heart condition or on medication? ask your doctor before using a sauna.

slides.title: heart health
slides.body: big finnish studies link regular sauna use with lower heart disease risk. a link, mind you, not proof. but promising.

slides.title: blood pressure
slides.body: studies show blood pressure tends to drop for a while after a sauna session.

slides.title: muscles
slides.body: heat helps tight muscles relax, which is why so many go after training.

slides.title: mood
slides.body: early research suggests heat may help mood. more studies are on the way. watch this space.

slides.title: not a cure
slides.body: sauna is a splendid habit, not a medicine. enjoy it for what it is.

stories.hook: sauna vs steam room vs infrared
stories.question: team sauna or team steam room?

slides.title: sauna: dry heat
slides.body: usually 70–100°C with dry air. chuck water on the hot stones and whoosh: a burst of steam called löyly.

slides.title: steam room: wet heat
slides.body: only about 40–50°C, but close to 100% humidity. feels like a tropical summit. sweltering.

slides.title: infrared: warms you, not the air
slides.body: the room stays around 45–60°C. gentler, so people tend to linger.

slides.title: so which is best?
slides.body: the one you'll actually go to. try all three. a coalition of heat, if you like.

stories.hook: london was sweating centuries before it was cool
stories.question: which old london bathhouse should we dig up next?
stories.note: pictures: hogarth (public domain); illustrated london news and st giles bagnio via wellcome collection (cc by 4.0); bishopsgate kiosk by herry lawford (cc by 2.0).

slides.title: the 1600s: bagnios
slides.body: london's first hot baths. hogarth set this scene in one: a husband skewered by his wife's lover, who legs it out the window. hardly relaxing.

slides.title: 1862: jermyn street
slides.body: the victorians went utterly potty for turkish baths. this hot room in st james's was the toast of the town, until a wartime bomb did for it.

slides.title: 1895: bishopsgate
slides.body: nevill's turkish baths, tucked off bishopsgate. city chaps sweated here, then toddled back to the office. marvellous.

slides.title: it's still there
slides.body: the little tiled kiosk survives in bishopsgate churchyard, a stone's throw from liverpool street. go and gawp, folks.

stories.caption:
london was sweating centuries before it was cool. a short history of the city's steam rooms, part 1.

1. bagnios. london's first hot baths, from the 1600s. hogarth set this scene from marriage a-la-mode (about 1743) in one: a husband run through by his wife's lover, who flees out of the window. by then 'bagnio' had a rather racy reputation, cripes.

2. jermyn street, 1862. the victorians went utterly potty for turkish baths. this is the hot room of the hammam in st james's, drawn for the illustrated london news. a wartime bomb finished it off.

3. bishopsgate, 1895. nevill's turkish baths opened just off bishopsgate. this is one of its cooling rooms, where city chaps lounged about after the hot rooms.

4. the tiled entrance kiosk, little dome and all, still stands in bishopsgate churchyard, a stone's throw from liverpool street. go and gawp, folks.
